newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Transport Council debates French trucks, Swiss.
newsitem.headline: Transport Council debates French trucks, Swiss.

text.p: The Transport Council began a regular meeting on Thursday to discuss items including truck transit problems through Switzerland and compensation claims from the recent French truckers' strike.

Ministers began their meeting with talks about the future of EU railways and European Commission proposals for reviving the flagging sector and reversing its steep loss of freight traffic to road hauliers in recent years.
"They are due to discuss relations with Switzerland this afternoon and the French truckers' strike over lunch," a spokesman for the Irish EU presidency told reporters.
"Certainly the question of compensation will come up," the diplomat added in reference to lunchtime closed-door talks.
Road hauliers in France's EU partner countries have sought compensation from Paris as a result of spoiled loads and delays from being caught in striking truckers' road blocks.
Switzerland and the EU's 15 countries have spent months discussing closer ties in a range of areas such as research, trade in processed farm products and free movement of people.

While most areas have been resolved, problems remain in liberalising road transport. The EU wants immediate access to Swiss roads for its 40-tonne lorries while Berne seeks a differentiated charging system penalising dirtier trucks in return for giving up its 28-tonne maximum-weight limit.
